title: Zul'Drak
body: Zul'Drak is the heartland of the Drakkari, the ice trolls of Northrend: a vast temple city of ziggurats, walls and aqueducts climbing in great tiers between the Grizzly Hills, Crystalsong Forest and the Storm Peaks, with Gundrak, the capital of their empire, at its heart. The empire is dying. The Scourge has pressed in from every side, raising necropolises over the lower tiers and taking Drak'Tharon Keep on the southern border, and in their desperation the Drakkari have turned on their own animal gods, slaying them at their great altars so that their prophets may drink the gods' power. Between the two stands the Argent Crusade, holding the Argent Stand and Light's Breach against both, while death knights of the Ebon Blade keep watch from Ebon Watch and Zandalari trolls, come from Zandalar to defend the gods who still live, hold a refuge at Zim'Torga.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Zul'Drak (temple city of ziggurats, walls and aqueducts between the Grizzly Hills, Crystalsong Forest and the Storm Peaks; Gundrak the capital; Argent Stand, Light's Breach, Ebon Watch, Zim'Torga)

notes: AREA 66. Opening is the zone as anyone arriving sees it; Drak'Tharon Keep and Gundrak named only (instances). The gods' deaths are the zone's premise, told by Lantinga's and Rimblat's open gossip, not an outcome of a chain; no single god's fate is named. Nothing after 3.3.5 (no Cataclysm Zul or later ruin). Checked: verified.

title: Light's Breach
body: Light's Breach is an Argent Crusade camp southwest of the Argent Stand, raised among ruins where every troll is now dead or fled to the upper tiers. The Scourge have forced their way between it and the Argent Stand, leaving Sergeant Riannah and her soldiers to hold out alone, and the Crusade has called fighters from across Northrend to her, warning that the Scourge are making a push to take all of Zul'Drak. Crusader Lord Lantinga commands here. Wolvar of the Rageclaw tribe, driven from their den by trolls, shelter in the camp with their pups, their chief and their elder shaman Moky.

title: Rageclaw Den
body: Southeast of Light's Breach lies Rageclaw Den, home of the Rageclaw wolvar, who lived beside the Drakkari for generations, allies for thousands of years and unaware of how the world was changing around them. Then the trolls fell on the den. Its huts burn, captured wolvar sit shackled in the village, and trolls calling themselves the Drakuru hold the ground. Even Ragemane, the chief's trusty lion seal, has turned on the hand that fed him and now haunts Rageclaw Lake beyond, and the heartbroken chief has posted a notice asking that he be put down.
sources: quest 12902 description (Rageclaw allied with the Drakkari for thousands of years; attack took them by surprise; den southeast)
quests 12859, 12861 descriptions (den burning; captured Rageclaw; trolls call themselves Drakuru trolls)

notes: AREA 4316 and 4374. Part 1 on DONE 12902, whose turn-in (the orders over the altar) and the next quest (12883, the orders' text) reveal who commands the attackers. Checked: Ragemane line kept to the notice (he bit the hand that fed him; the lake is where he is found); part 1 reworded to the orders' own claims (12883 description, shown at 12902's turn-in).

parts.body: The attack was no troll quarrel. Floating above a strange altar in the den were orders from Drakuru himself: the Lich King had given him full control of the Scourge's armies in Zul'Drak, his minions were to heed their master's call, and everything was to die.
sources: quest 12902 reward text (scroll floating above the strange altar)

title: Crusader Forward Camp
body: On the border of the Dead Fields stands the Crusader Forward Camp, sent out from Light's Breach days ago to open a battle front. Crusader Dargath, Crusader MacKellar, Engineer Reed and the twins Gerk and Burr established it with a steam tank, meant to carry the fight into the fields where the Scourge gather the dead. Their last word to Light's Breach was that the camp stood ready.
sources: quest 12894 description (Dargath, MacKellar, Reed and the twins Gerk and Burr sent to the Dead Fields; camp on the border, northwest of Light's Breach)
quest 12894 description (last correspondence: camp successfully established)
notes: AREA 4489 and ACCEPT 12894 (Lantinga's quest, both factions). The opening is the camp as Lantinga knows it; the attack is part 1 (DONE 12894, MacKellar's reward text) and the search's end part 2 (DONE 12903); Gerk's own account (12904) is told in 6604. Checked: removed the tank as 'the camp's pride and best hope' (unsupported, and on arrival the tank is already wrecked); added Lantinga's last report. Thrym's End is now in 6605.

parts.body: Then the Scourge came. Prince Navarius led the attack, wrecked the tank and carried off Dargath, Gerk and Burr. MacKellar told how Dargath had the engine cut and charged out alone, saying someone had to leave the tank or they would all die. The camp, he found, sat in the middle of a Scourge factory.

The search for the three ended at Thrym's End and the ruins beyond it, and none of them came home. MacKellar swore that the great sacrifice they made would not soon be forgotten and would not be in vain. Of the camp's founders, only he and Engineer Reed remain.
sources: quest 12903 description and reward text (great sacrifice of the three; not in vain)

title: The Dead Fields and Thrym's End
body: The Dead Fields stretch north of Light's Breach, and they are well named. Corpses lie in rows, the reanimated dead stir among them and banshee soulclaimers drift overhead. The Scourge run the fields as a factory, gathering the dead of Zul'Drak to be sent up to the necropolis Zeramas, where Prince Navarius and his crew make them into Scourge. At their edge lie the ruins now called Dargath's Demise. Northwest of the Crusader Forward Camp, Thrym's End is a base of the Scourge's vargul, strewn with scrap from their arrival. On tables at its far side they experiment on the dead, and in a hundred foot cage they hold a storm giant who rages at his captors.

parts.body: A dying crusader named Gerk told what the vargul are: those the Lich King did not find worthy. He bid whoever heard him imagine how strong the worthy must be, and prayed that they would never have to face them in number.

title: Ebon Watch
body: Ebon Watch is the camp of the Knights of the Ebon Blade in western Zul'Drak, raised to hunt the Scourge they once served. Stefan Vadu commands it, holding that none know the Scourge better than death knights and that the best weapon against fire is fire. Beside him Bloodrose Datura keeps a captured Drakkari scout under guard. The knights' own suppliers, with names like Corpsedust, Deathdrip and Squirmworm, keep them provisioned.
sources: zone_areas 4312 (Stefan Vadu 28518, Bloodrose Datura 28532, Captured Drakkari Scout 28541, Corrosion, Spiked, Mulch, Deathdrip, Corpsedust, Scabbard, Squirmworm, Baneflight 28615, Ebon Watch Guardian)

title: Voltarus
body: Over the blighted pools of northwestern Zul'Drak hang two necropolises. Voltarus hovers above the Reliquary of Pain, where blight geists harvest crystals of blight from the earth, bloated abominations and servants of Drakuru lurch among blight cauldrons and scourgewagons, and blightguards watch for anything that does not belong. It is the seat of Overlord Drakuru. To the southwest, east of Ebon Watch, Zeramas hangs over the Reliquary of Agony, where ghouls and abominations wallow and a Scourge merchant named Gristlegut feeds the ghouls. North of Voltarus, at the Frigid Breach, a Drakkari army has broken through the wall.

parts.body: The necropolis keeps its secret in an upper chamber. There, beside Drakkari chieftains caged after the fighting at the Frigid Breach, stand Drakuru's secret weapons: Blightblood trolls, the makings of what he calls the ultimate Scourge army, with which he means to take the palace of Gundrak.

title: The Argent Stand
body: The Argent Stand is the Argent Crusade's stronghold in the lower city, a terrace above a courtyard where the fighting against the Scourge never ends and sky terrors snatch crusaders into the air. Commander Kunz drills every newcomer, Commander Falstaav holds the line between the Scourge on one side and the Drakkari rituals on the other, and Hexxer Ubungo of the Zandalar tribe counsels them. Among the others are Crusade Commander Korfax, who told the highlord it was a mistake to come and is overdue in Icecrown, the shaman Rimblat Earthshatter, Rayne, who thought nothing could be worse than the battle for Light's Hope Chapel, Avenger Metz and the old orc Eitrigg.
sources: zone_areas 4275 (Kunz 28039, Falstaav 28059, Ubungo 28062, Korfax 28175, Rimblat 28176, Rayne 28177, Metz 28178, Eitrigg 28244, Sky Terror, Argent Crusader)
quests 12503 (courtyard below, no end to the fighting), 12740 (sky terrors drop crusaders)

npc_text 13043 (Kunz), 13046 (Falstaav), 13050 (Ubungo, Zandalar tribe), 14284 (Korfax: overdue in Icecrown, told the highlord it was a mistake), 14285 (Rimblat), 14286 (Rayne: the Plaguelands and Light's Hope)
notes: AREA 4275 and TALK 28244 (Eitrigg's Zul'Drak creature: one spawn, here, gossip; not 3144). Eitrigg is mentioned only (Orgrimmar 163709 part 2 tells his service and that the saronite goes to Fordring); part 1 tells the test of the ore by his companions, which Orgrimmar does not. No Tirion entry. Checked: part 1 no longer says the ore goes to the highlord (Orgrimmar 163709 part 2 tells that); it ends on Eitrigg's vow instead. The scene runs on 12584's reward (smart_scripts 28244).

parts.body: Captain Rupert sent for saronite from the fallen necropolis, and when it reached the Stand, Eitrigg's companions put it to the test. Korfax's axe failed to scratch it, Rimblat's call to the elements did nothing, Rayne swore nature could not touch it, and when Metz called on the Light the blast knocked them all back. Its secrets, Eitrigg vowed, would yet be unlocked, before it was too late.
sources: smart_scripts 28244 (scene on Pure Evil reward) and 2824400

title: Altar of Sseratus
body: At the end of the avenue north of the Argent Stand rises the Altar of Sseratus, the snake god's holy place. Its priests, champions and snake handlers still crowd the steps, and a prophet holds court before the main building, boasting that with the power of the wild gods in their veins not even the Lich King can stand against them. An Argent Crusade force under Sergeant Stackhammer is deployed before the altar, where the soldiers warn one another that these trolls are bad news.
sources: quest 12505 description (altar up the avenue, Stackhammer)
quest 12506 description (altar of the snake god; avoid the prophet)
zone_areas 4276 (Priest, Champion of Sseratus, Snake Handler, Prophet 28068, Sseratus 28089, Stackhammer 28056, Corporal Maga 28099, Argent Soldier)
notes: AREA 4276. The soldier line about the trolls killing their own snake god is left out of the opening: Sseratus's death is the reveal of 12506 (part 1). Part 2 on DONE 12516. Checked: verified; 'spreading' softened to the reward text's 'occurring up in the higher tiers'.

parts.body: Inside the main building lies Sseratus, slain by his own worshippers. They have drunk deeply of his mojo, the prophet most of all, and Hexxer Ubungo, his spirit visibly lowered by the news, knew the prophet had to be stopped before he drank much more.

Ubungo had the god's mojo spiked with elemental fluids and muddlecap fungus, and the prophet, arrogant as ever, drank it when it was thrown to him. Muddled and weakened, he was slain, and the hexxer warned that the same madness was loose in the higher tiers.

title: Drak'Sotra
body: Drak'Sotra lies southeast of the Argent Stand, and the Crusade has paid dearly for it. Pushed back and driven from the ruins by the Scourge, its soldiers hold the wall under Captain Rupert, while Captain Brandon raises the Crusade's banners to lift their spirits and Dr. Rogers waits for the wounded. Their own dead rise against them, nerubians tunnel up from below, and cowering recruits fight on. To the west lie the Drak'Sotra Fields, where the trolls grow water poppies and water elementals have flooded in through a weakened wall between worlds, followed by Drakkari shamans come down to bind them.
sources: quest 12512 description (pushed back; lost Drak'Sotra to the Scourge; find the wounded)
quests 12502, 12509, 12568, 12598 descriptions (banners, cowering recruits, burning the fallen, nerubian tunnels)

title: Kolramas
body: Southeast of Drak'Sotra lies Kolramas, a Scourge necropolis that the Drakkari somehow brought down out of the sky. Its wreck crashed almost on the Crusade's doorstep, and it did not kill everything inside. Hath'ar nerubians crawl through its innards, necromagi raise the fallen crusaders as Scourge, plague sprayers hover over the ruins, and Malas the Corrupter gloats from atop the wreck. The necropolis was carrying saronite when it fell, and chunks of the ore lie strewn through its insides.
sources: quest 12552 description (trolls brought down Kolramas; it crashed next to us; raising our men)
npc_text 13117 (Moonshard: how did they manage to do that)
quest 12554 description (Malas the Corrupter gloating atop)

parts.body: Malas the Corrupter did not gloat for long. He was slain atop the wreck and his head brought back to Sergeant Moonshard, who meant to mount it on a pike so it could never rise again, and who kicked it away in disgust.
sources: quest 12554 description, request and reward text

parts.body: Specialist Cogwheel found a use for the nerubians' own silk. A tangled skein thrower built from their spinnerets fouled the plague sprayers' hover spells until they crashed to the ground, just as Kolramas had, and the specialist was glad not to be sprayed with Scourge filth.

title: Heb'Valok and Drak'Agal
body: North of the Argent Stand, the Crusade holds the shrine of Heb'Valok, where Alchemist Finklestein, the Crusade's finest, has set up his laboratory and keeps Captain Arnath gathering his reagents, to the captain's dismay. South of it, at the Pools of Zha'Jin, the spirits of ancient trolls drift over the water. East of the Stand lies Drak'Agal, a sector of stagnant, flooded ruins where Captain Grondel's soldiers fight knee deep in water among basilisks and sewage elementals, burning dead thornwood roots to stay dry.
sources: quest 12799 description (Finklestein the Crusade's best alchemist; pools of spirits of ancient trolls just south)
quests 12599, 12594 descriptions (Grondel: knee-deep in stagnant water; thornwood; sewage elementals)
zone_areas 4294 (Finklestein 28205, Arnath 28045, reagents), 4280, 4318 (Lost Drakkari Spirit, Disturbed Soul)
notes: AREA 4294, 4280 and 4318. Part 1 on DONE 12541 or 12601/12602 (the truth serum); 12601 and 12602 have no starter, so only 12541 is used. Checked: verified.

parts.body: Finklestein's laboratory serves the war. A Drakkari prisoner was sent to him for questioning, and with a hurried assistant fetching ingredients at his shouted command, he brewed the truth serum for the interrogation, sure that what the troll told would be of great value.

title: The Forgotten Gods
body: Not every god of Zul'Drak lies on a bloodied altar. Some stand as great statues the Drakkari once honored with offerings and now neglect. Zim'Abwa, southwest of the Argent Stand, stares unmoving to the north and the south. Zim'Torga, the Mother of Prosperity, shelters the Zandalari in her shadow. Zim'Rhuk, called the Wise One, stands to the north of her, protected by giant guardians who deal harshly with intruders. Hexxer Ubungo and Witch Doctor Khufu teach that the gods still answer offerings of Drakkari artifacts with their blessing.
sources: quests 12565, 12615, 12655 descriptions and texts (neglected gods; Zim'Abwa southwest of the Stand; Zim'Torga Mother of Prosperity; Zim'Rhuk the Wise One, protective, guardians)
notes: AREA 4319 and 4328, ACCEPT 12565, 12615, 12655 (none auto-complete: QuestType 2). The repeatable blessings 12567, 12618, 12656 (QuestType 0) are not used. Zim'Torga's own subzone is 6615. The blessings' reward texts are used only as sources (each tells one god, so no part). Checked: verified. 12565, 12615, 12655 are QuestType 2, flags 136, SpecialFlags 0: not repeatable, not auto-complete.

title: Amphitheater of Anguish
body: In the middle of the lower city stands the Amphitheater of Anguish, a great coliseum of the Drakkari. Its newest masters are not trolls at all. The goblin Gurgthock and his troll bodyguard Wodin, who ran the Ring of Blood in Nagrand, have come north and opened a fight club here, with spectators in the stands and vendors selling snacks. Challengers fight whatever Gurgthock can find, and once a bout begins, no one leaves the arena: win or die.
sources: quest 12974 description (Gurgthock and Wodin from the Ring of Blood, new fight club in Zul'Drak, big arena in the center)
quest 12932 description (Gurgthock fight promoter, Wodin his bodyguard)

title: Zim'Torga
body: Up the great steps northeast of the Argent Stand, on the next tier of the city, lies Zim'Torga, a refuge the Zandalari have taken in the presence of the statue of Zim'Torga, Mother of Prosperity. Witch Doctor Khufu leads them, Element-Tamer Dagoda binds captured elementals as defenders, Scalper Ahunae swings his axe at any troll who comes close, and Chronicler To'kini records the fall of the empire. The refuge is under constant attack from the Drakkari, and the goddess herself has been weakened by the Scourge and by her own people.
sources: quest 12623 description (Zim'Torga up the great steps to the northeast; refuge the Zandalari defend; constant attack)
quest 12615 description (refuge within the presence of Zim'Torga, Mother of Prosperity)
npc_text 13180 (Dagoda: Zim'Torga weakened by the Scourge and the Drakkari), 13234 (Ahunae), 13282 (To'kini)

TALK 28401 is not used to prove it: the same entry also stands at her altar before 12685. parts.body: Har'koa herself now dwells in Zim'Torga. After giving up a portion of her spirit so that Quetz'lun could be avenged, the snow leopard goddess left her altar for the Zandalari refuge, and it is from here that she calls on her champion for the work still to be done.
sources: spell_area 52484 (area 4323, from 12685 rewarded) and 52485 (area 4322, until 12685 rewarded); Spell.dbc: both are invisibility detection, type 8, matching her two spawns' auras 52483 and 51666

title: Pools of Jin'Alai and Heb'Drakkar
body: Southwest of Zim'Torga lie the Pools of Jin'Alai, where Drakkari warriors gather under their leaders and medicine men stir four great cauldrons in rituals that block the Zandalari from speaking with the gods. To the northeast the trolls of Heb'Drakkar keep a bat rookery, from which their headhunters and strikers raid the refuge on bats while their leader Heb'Jin goads them on from atop the rookery.
sources: quest 12622 description (trolls gathered at the pools; their leaders)
quest 12627 description (medicine men's rituals interfere; cauldrons)
quests 12659, 12662 descriptions (Heb'Drakkar northeast; bat rookery; Heb'Jin goading his forces; his drum)

parts.body: The cauldrons were overturned and the medicine men's ritual broke. At once Khufu could feel the difference, and he turned again to the gods to ask what must be done to save them.

title: Altar of Har'koa
body: Southeast of Zim'Torga stands the Altar of Har'koa, the snow leopard goddess. She is the last of the gods to be subdued, and her subduers hold her there with their magic while her claws guard the grounds, they and the subduers alike once her own supplicants. Worse, her own offspring have been twisted into cursed monstrosities that prowl the altar. Har'koan relics lie scattered across it, and a prophet of Har'koa waits among the trolls.
sources: quest 12632 description (last of the gods to be subdued; bound by magic; offspring transformed into monstrosities)
zone_areas 4322 (Har'koa 28401, Har'koan Subduer, Claw of Har'koa, Cursed Offspring, Prophet of Har'koa 28848, Har'koan Relic)
notes: AREA 4322. Har'koa leaves the altar for Zim'Torga with 12685 (spell_area 52485 here until 12685 rewarded): part 1 on DONE 12685. Checked: part 1 no longer says her weakness made her withdraw (no source gives a reason).

parts.body: Har'koa no longer waits at her altar. Already weakened by her subduers, she gave a portion of her spirit for Quetz'lun's revenge, and afterward she left for the Zandalari refuge at Zim'Torga, leaving the grounds to the trolls who had bound her.

title: Altar of Rhunok
body: Northwest of Zim'Torga, beyond the broken tundra of Drak'Mabwa, stands the Altar of Rhunok, the arctic bear god. His priests keep his body close to death inside the altar building, where a tormentor keeps him weak so that a prophet can finish draining him, and they have plundered their own holy site. On the tundra below, rifts in the frozen ground pour out elementals of frozen earth, and a prophet of Rhunok lies in a water-filled crater, tended by priests.
sources: npc_text 13291 (body kept close to death in the altar building)
creature_text 28575 (tormentor: keep him weak so the prophet can finish)
quest 12650 description (plundered their own holy site)
quests 12639, 12640 (frozen earth, elemental rifts at Drak'Mabwa)
quest 12646 description (crater to the south in Drak'Mabwa)
notes: AREA 4321 and 4327. Opening keeps the prophet's state vague (the crater and the priests are visible); his self-destruction is told by the spirit in 12642's turn-in and 12646 (part 1). Part 2 on DONE 12647. Checked: verified.

parts.body: Rhunok's spirit had already left his weakened body. It told how his prophet drank too much of his power too quickly and died of it, and how the priests were raising him again to finish the work. The resurrected prophet was slain and the bear god's mojo taken back.

Rhunok's body was too far gone to save. Imbued with the last of his power, a mortal woke the body with the tormentor's incense and slew it, as the god himself asked, so that no new prophet could finish what the first began. The god thanked his slayer for the honor, and hoped that they and Har'koa could still help the others.
sources: quest 12653 description and reward text (we are eternal; his spirit will live on)

title: Altars of Quetz'lun and Mam'toth
body: East of Zim'Torga rises the Altar of Quetz'lun, the wind serpent goddess, and it has been overrun: her scions and great altar wardens circle the grounds, worshippers and serpent-touched berserkers fill them, and a prophet of Quetz'lun holds the altar. Something is wrong with the goddess, though not even Har'koa can sense what. North of the altar opens a vast crater where the blood of Mam'toth, the mammoth god, still lives, and beyond it, up the steps to the next tier, lies what is left of his altar. Much of the temple is simply gone, and enraged mammoths roam among his disciples, living and dead.
sources: quest 12665 description (something wrong with Quetz'lun; altar overrun with powerful creatures)
zone_areas 4325 (Scion of Quetz'lun, Altar Warden, Quetz'lun Worshipper, Serpent-Touched Berserker, Prophet 28671, Quetz'lun 28672)
quest 12707 description (what's left of the Altar of Mam'toth; enraged mammoths; disciples)
quest 12684 description (crater north of the Altar of Quetz'lun; his blood yet lives)
zone_areas 4329 (Dead Mam'toth Disciple, Mam'toth Disciple, Enraged Mammoth), 4371 (Blood of Mam'toth 28779)
creature positions: Blood of Mam'toth (x 6018) north of the altar (x 5717), Mam'toth Disciples (x 6259) beyond
notes: AREA 4325, 4371 and 4329. Checked: the Altar of Mam'toth (former 6620, dropped) merged in to bring the places nearer the usual range. Phases: 51671 (Ghostly, phase 2: the underworld) from 12667 complete until 12675 rewarded, told as past in story 6632 on DONE 12668; 52351 (Quetz'lun's Protection, faction 1065) from DONE 12675 on, a lasting change, part 1 on DONE 12675 (its description promises it). Part 2 on ACCEPT 12684 (its description); the request text's lament (nothing can bring him back) dropped, as it shows only at the turn-in. Her death and the prophet's end are in 6632.

parts.body: Quetz'lun's spirit keeps her word. Since a mortal served her in her underworld and carried her plea to Har'koa, her scions and wardens no longer fall upon that servant, and the way through the altar grounds to her prophet lies open.
sources: spell_area 52351 (Quetz'lun's Protection in 4325 from 12675 rewarded; faction 1065)
quest 12675 description (children and guardians will no longer attack you)

parts.body: Mam'toth was not slain like the other gods. Har'koa tells how, rather than let his trolls gain his power, he destroyed himself and took much of his temple with him, leaving the crater behind. His blood still lives there, and with it she means to bolster herself before she gives up a portion of her own spirit.
sources: quest 12684 description (Mam'toth destroyed himself rather than let his trolls gain his power; crater; his blood yet lives; bolster herself before sacrificing a portion of her spirit)

title: Zol'Maz Stronghold
body: Up the steps northeast of Zim'Torga stands Zol'Maz Stronghold, the seat of the Drakkari warlord Zol'Maz and his family. Its gate is guarded by enchanted tiki warriors, his special guardians, which the Zandalari fear could overrun them if the Drakkari made them in numbers. The warlord is said to be deeply paranoid, and he has hexed all of the stronghold's caches with dire magic.
sources: quest 12708 description (enchanted tiki warriors, special guardians, mass production)
quest 12709 description (warlord extremely paranoid; caches hexed)
quest 12712 description (stronghold up the steps to the northeast; warlord and family; gate)
zone_areas 4372 (Warlord Zol'Maz 28902, Tiri, Yara, Drek'Maz, Enchanted Tiki Warrior, Zol'Maz Stronghold Cache, Zol'Maz Gate)
notes: AREA 4372. The caches' revelation is in 6630 part 1 (DONE 12709); the warlord's death is part 1 here (DONE 12712). Checked: 'the champion hunting the gods' tormentors' made plain (12712: hearing of your exploits).

parts.body: Warlord Zol'Maz carried the key to the chains of Akali, the rhino god. Hearing of the deeds of Har'koa's champion, he shut himself and his family in the stronghold. His family fell first, their tiki, sword and incantation called up help before his gate, and the warlord, raging at their deaths, fell there. The key was taken.

title: Gundrak and Dubra'Jin
body: Gundrak is the capital of the Drakkari Empire, a great palace city, and its trolls, fire-eaters, brutes and bat riders, swarm its approaches. In the courtyard before its gates Akali, the rhino god, lies in chains at four anchor points while his subduers prepare him for slaughter. Just south lies Zol'Heb with its circle of power. Beside the city a few Zandalari keep watch from the post of Dubra'Jin, observing the Drakkari and recording what they see.
sources: quest 12721 description (Akali held in the courtyard before Gundrak, capital of Zul'Drak; four anchor points; teeming with ice trolls)
quest 12730 description (Zol'Heb just south of Gundrak; circle of power)
quest 13099 description (post just west of Gundrak)
zone_areas 4375 (Akali 28952, Akali Subduer, Gundrak Fire-eater, Brute, Bat Rider, Akali Chain Anchor), 4373, 4579 (Tol'mar, Bah'Kini, Ha'wana)
quest 13096 offer text (Tol'mar's job to observe only)
notes: AREA 4375, 4373 and 4579. The inner city is an instance: named only; 13096, 13098 and 13111 (QuestSortID 4416) not used. Part 1 on DONE 12721 (Akali freed and slain). Checked: the raptor-egg offerings to Dubra'Jin removed (13556 and Ha'wana 33025 are 3.1 content, state 14); the post is told from 13099 and 13096 (observing and recording). Akali 28952 stands in phase 1.

parts.body: Akali was set free, and he roared that the Drakkari would pay for their trespasses. Then the prophet of Akali stepped in and slew the rhino god, claiming his blood for his master and some of his power for himself, sending the one who freed him back to Har'koa with a warning that he was coming for her next.

title: Overlord Drakuru
body: Overlord Drakuru commands the Scourge in Zul'Drak from the necropolis Voltarus. He is a Drakkari himself, and by his own orders the Lich King has given him full control of the Scourge armies here: the dead of the Dead Fields go up to Zeramas to be made into Scourge, the trolls who follow him call themselves the Drakuru, and he promises that he will soon drink the blood of the prophets and see Zul'Drak and Gundrak fall. The Ebon Blade have tracked him since the Grizzly Hills and mean to see him destroyed.
sources: quest 12884 reward text (tracking Drakuru since the Grizzly Hills; slated for eradication)
npc_text 13348 (another supplicant seeking the Lich King's favors)
notes: TALK 28503 (one spawn, Voltarus; met only in disguise; his gossip 13348 calls the visitor another supplicant of the Lich King), DONE 12884, ACCEPT 12664 and 12663 (his own quests, both acceptable only with 12661 in the log). Picks up from grizzly_hills.json 39429 without retelling it; his reveal inside Drak'Tharon (12238, instance) is not told. Checked: the opening's tie to the Lich King is shown to every route in (12883 orders, 12664 and 12663 greetings, gossip 13348), so it stays. Prerequisites: the choker chain splits on 12238 by loot conditions (Unliving Choker 38660 only without 12238, Writhing Choker 38673 only with it): 12631 > 12637 > 12629 > 12648 > 12664, or 12633 > 12638 > 12643 > 12649 > 12663; 12661 needs 12648 or 12649; then 12669 > 12677 > 12676 > 12713, with 12686, 12690 and 12710 from Drakuru alongside. Every part is reachable in the open world except part 1 (ACCEPT 12663), which only characters who did the instance quest 12238 reach; the others get part 2 through 12664. Part 3 no longer says the chieftains are steeped in blight (unsupported) and no longer cites creature_text 28998 groups 0-1 (spoken only in the 12713 scene). Part 4 checked against zone_zuldrak.cpp npc_overlord_drakuru_betrayal: Drakuru's lines 2-7, the portal crystal, the Lich King 28498 summoned, his lines 7-12 and Touch of Death; the part tells only that.

parts.body: To those who once helped him in the Grizzly Hills, Drakuru speaks as an old friend. The choker that called them to Voltarus was his gift, he says: they have come a long way together, and now they serve the Lich King side by side. Big things, he promises, are coming.

From Voltarus he sends new servants on a tour of his domain, his voice following them: part of the land is already his, the self-righteous crusaders will fall, the Drakkari are destroying their own lands, and Gundrak is his destiny, which they will help him conquer.

His master plan is an army. The Drakkari chieftains taken at the Frigid Breach went to his upper chamber, where his Blightblood trolls wait, and with this ultimate Scourge army he means to sweep through the swarms of Drakkari and take his rightful place in the palace of Gundrak, to the Lich King's great pleasure.

Drakuru's trust was his undoing. His Blightbloods were turned against him, and beaten, he called on his master. The Lich King came, but only to condemn him for his failure and strike him dead. The betrayer he spared, amused, with a warning that next time he would require much more.

title: Har'koa
body: Har'koa is the snow leopard goddess of the Drakkari, and by her own account the last of Zul'Drak's gods to be subdued. When the Zandalari were sent to her, her own trolls held her at her altar southeast of Zim'Torga, bound by the magic of her subduers so that she could not even discern the fates of the other gods, and they had turned her magic against her by twisting her offspring into monstrosities. To the Zandalari she is the one the gods themselves pointed them to, and she speaks with urgency: time is short.
sources: quest 12632 description (last of the gods to be subdued; bound; offspring transformed)
quest 12628 description and reward text (the gods have spoken; speak with the leopard goddess; time is of the essence)
creature 28401 (spawns at the Altar of Har'koa and Zim'Torga, both in Zul'Drak)
notes: TALK 28401 and DONE 12628. Checked: 28401 has two spawns, both in Zul'Drak and phase 1, each hidden by an invisibility aura (51666 at the altar, 52483 at Zim'Torga) that the player sees only through spell_area 52485 (4322, until 12685 rewarded) or 52484 (4323, from 12685 rewarded); so she can be talked to at the altar before 12685 and at Zim'Torga after. The opening is now told as she was when the Zandalari came to her, so it is true in both places and after part 2. 'Last still unsubdued' corrected to her own words (the last of the gods to be subdued). Part 1 (DONE 12632) no longer repeats the opening. Part 2 on DONE 12685 (the move), part 3 on DONE 12730 (creature_text 29050).

parts.body: Her tortured children were slain and, by the magic of her whisker, brought back to life free of their nightmare, and she swore never to forget it. With that kindness done she turned to her purpose: the other gods were to be freed before herself.

For Quetz'lun's revenge she gave up a portion of her own spirit, though it was a costly gift when she was already so weak, bolstering herself with the living blood of Mam'toth. Afterward she left her altar for the Zandalari refuge at Zim'Torga.

When the prophet of Akali was called to Zol'Heb, Har'koa feared she would not see her champion again until the afterlife. Yet in the end she came herself, ordering the prophet to keep his hands off them and break his ritual, and thanked them for saving everyone once more.

title: Witch Doctor Khufu
body: Witch Doctor Khufu leads the Zandalari at Zim'Torga. He grieves to see the Drakkari destroy themselves, warning that the power they win by killing the gods of the land is fleeting and will be lost to them for all eternity. He tries to commune with the gods and beseeches them for guidance, but the medicine men of the Pools of Jin'Alai work rituals that block him, and he sends any willing help against them.
sources: npc_text 13176 (power transitory, lost for all eternity)
quest 12627 description (communing with the gods; medicine men interfering)
notes: TALK 28479 (one spawn, Zim'Torga) and DONE 12623 (turned in to him). Part 1 on DONE 12721 (turned in to him: Akali's death, and he consults the gods again, 12729). Checked: part 1 moved from DONE 12721 to ACCEPT 12729: the gods' answer is 12729's description (12721 offers no next quest), and 12729 requires 12721, whose reward text gives the rest.

parts.body: When Akali was slain and his prophet sent his threat, Khufu was stricken: another god destroyed, its power stolen, and the prophet coming for Har'koa. He turned once more to the gods, and they answered with the means to force the prophet out.

title: Crusader Lord Lantinga
body: Crusader Lord Lantinga commands the Argent Crusade at Light's Breach. He would have every newcomer look around and let the devastation sink in: the trolls who lived here are dead or fled, and the Drakkari, in a desperate bid to hold back the Scourge, sacrificed their own gods and drank their blood, leaving the ancient empire in ruin. Half of the Crusade's army is tied down at the Argent Stand, and he wants answers about the attack on the Rageclaw.
sources: quest 12883 reward text (half our army tied up at the Argent Stand)
notes: TALK 29687 (one spawn, Light's Breach) and ACCEPT 12902. Part 1 on DONE 12883 (his reaction to the orders). Checked: verified.

parts.body: The orders from the Rageclaw den bore a name he knew: if this was the same Drakuru from Drak'Tharon Keep, the Crusade would need help. Grudgingly he sent word to the death knights of Ebon Watch, muttering that he had hoped never to see those scoundrels again after Light's Hope.

title: Stefan Vadu
body: Stefan Vadu, a death knight of the Knights of the Ebon Blade, commands Ebon Watch. He has little patience for the Argent Crusade, which he says is late to the party once again, and none for doubt: none know the Scourge better than death knights. His methods are his own. He keeps Nass, a servant so steeped in blight that he is deaf, blind and all but immune to it, and he is not above turning the Scourge's own ways against them.
sources: quest 12884 reward text (Argent Crusade late to the party; tracking Drakuru)
quest 12629 description (use their desires against them)
notes: TALK 28518 (one spawn, Ebon Watch) and DONE 12884. A death knight figure with no entry elsewhere (flagged): only his Zul'Drak work is told; his later appearance in Icecrown Citadel (instance) is left out. No parts: his operation is story 6631. Nass (28521) is a summoned humanoid; called only a servant. Checked: no Stefan Vadu entry in any finished zone file; the last line no longer previews 12629's plan. Prince Navarius and Algar appear only inside other entries, with no KILL.

title: Gymer
body: Gymer is the king of the storm giants, and a prisoner of the Scourge at Thrym's End. He came to Zul'Drak at a cry for help from his brother Thiassi, only to find too late that it was a trap: Thiassi is now an undead servant of the Lich King. Gymer fears he will soon share the fate of many other storm giants. To a stranger who does not reek of death, he offers his help in return for his freedom.
sources: quest 12919 description (flesh giants from storm giant corpses; Thrym)
notes: TALK 29647 (one spawn, Thrym's End, gossip) and ACCEPT 12912. Part 1 on DONE 12916 (freed), part 2 on DONE 12919 (the rampage). Navarius, Algar and Thrym stand in phase 256 only, so no KILL is used. Checked: the flesh giants moved from the opening to part 1 (they are told in 12919, offered at 12916's turn-in; 12912 says only that he fears the fate of other storm giants).

parts.body: Engineer Reed's jumbo seaforium charge broke the hinges of his cage, and Gymer kept his word. Like the mortals, he wishes to see the Scourge driven from this land and the Lich King destroyed. The Scourge have decimated his people, stitching their corpses into flesh giants or worse, aberrations like Thrym, and he vowed that Navarius, Algar and Thrym would all die.

With a rider on his head, the storm king marched into the heart of the Scourge in Zul'Drak and smashed it. Algar the Chosen, the stitched giant Thrym and Prince Navarius all fell, and Crusader MacKellar called it a story for the ages.

title: Chronicler To'kini
body: Chronicler To'kini is a Zandalari scholar at Zim'Torga. While his companions take up arms, he holds that his people are chiefly here to witness what is happening and to chronicle the end of an empire. He gathers the relics the Drakkari neglect or plunder, so that the history of their empire is not lost with it, and he has little patience for the Drakkari themselves, brutal savages bent on their own demise.
sources: quest 12635 reward text (determined to bring about their own demise)
notes: TALK 28527 (one spawn, Zim'Torga) and ACCEPT 12635. Part 1 on DONE 12650 (PrevQuestID 12635, so both lessons have been heard), part 2 on DONE 13099 (Bah'Kini's verdict on him). Checked: the wildlife for Zandalar removed (13549 is 3.1 content, state 14); his view of the Drakkari added from 12650 and 12635.

parts.body: The relics teach as much as any book. The Drakkari, he explains, were exiled from the other troll nations for their extreme violence, which is how they came to so harsh a land, and one Rhunokian artifact shows the Sundering: Northrend was once the far north of Kalimdor, which is why Drakkari live in the south as well.
sources: quest 12650 reward text (12650 follows 12635, so its turn-in comes after both lessons)

parts.body: He calls Bah'Kini, who records events from a post beside Gundrak, his long-time student. She tells it differently: she is his daughter, sent there because her father was too fearful to take up a post so near Gundrak himself.

title: The Death of the Gods
body: The Scourge's presence has weakened the land of Zul'Drak, and with it the wild gods the Drakkari have worshipped for ages. The Drakkari saw their chance. At altar after altar their prophets have slain the very gods they served and drunk their mojo, and the power burning in them has let them strike back at the Scourge. The elements cry out that the land is almost dead, and the Zandalari, who have come to defend the gods who remain, warn that such power is fleeting and the Drakkari are bringing about their own doom.
sources: quest 12506 description (presence of the Scourge weakened the land and the wild gods; Drakkari take advantage)
quest 12623 description (Zandalari must stop what the Drakkari are doing to their gods)
notes: ACCEPT 12506, ACCEPT 12623 and TALK 28176 (Rimblat, one spawn at the Argent Stand). The opening is open setting. Each god's own fate is told by its place (6609, 6618, 6619, 6620, 6622) and Quetz'lun's in 6632; this entry tells why, and the end of the chain. Part 1 DONE 12709, part 2 DONE 12730, part 3 DONE 13097. Gal'darah named as 13096's offer text, shown at 13097's turn-in, names him; nothing of Gundrak's instance is told. Checked: part 2's 'champion of Zul'Drak' is Har'koa's word (12730 reward), not the Zandalari's. Part 3: 13097 offers 13096 at its turn-in (RewardNextQuest), whose text names Gal'darah and asks that he be sought in Gundrak; nothing of the instance or its outcome is told.

parts.body: The caches of Zol'Maz Stronghold held the reason. The Drakkari saw that the Scourge had weakened the land, and the warlord pushed his prophets to kill their gods so that they could seize the power and fight back against the Lich King's forces. Either way, Chronicler To'kini judged, they were doomed.

The prophet of Akali, swollen with the rhino god's power, swore that nothing would stand between him and Zim'Torga. Summoned to the circle of power at Zol'Heb, he boasted that a mere mortal could not defeat a god's might, and he fell all the same. Har'koa hailed his slayer as the champion of Zul'Drak.

Yet the greater part of Akali's blood had empowered another. Tol'mar of Dubra'Jin, sworn only to observe, could not stay silent after watching Akali slain before his eyes: Gal'darah, within Gundrak, must pay, he declared.

title: Infiltrating Voltarus
body: At Ebon Watch the Knights of the Ebon Blade have one target in Zul'Drak: Overlord Drakuru, whom they have followed since the Grizzly Hills. Reaching him is another matter, for he commands from a necropolis full of Scourge. The knights know the Scourge from within, having once served it themselves. Then a choker of bone, dripping with blood, turned up on a withered troll. Whoever found it felt a dark compulsion to put it on, and resisting the urge, brought it to Ebon Watch: if anyone could explain such a thing, a death knight could.
sources: creature_loot_template 28519 (Withered Troll: Unliving and Writhing Chokers)
notes: DONE 12884, ACCEPT 12631 and 12633 (the two choker paths; 12633 for those who did 12238). Parts: DONE 12637/12638 (Bloodrose's demonstration), DONE 12648/12649 (the disguise), DONE 12661 (inside Voltarus), DONE 12676 (the sabotage; 12669, 12677 and 12676 run in that order, so its turn-in follows all three), DONE 12713 (the end, told from the Ebon Blade side; Drakuru's death and the Lich King are in 6623 part 4). Checked: Stefan's verdict that the finder was chosen moved from the opening to part 1: it is 12631's and 12633's reward text, and the opening is earned on their accept. Both routes are open world (12631 without 12238, 12633 with it).

parts.body: Stefan knew such things. Its finder, he said, had been chosen. Bloodrose Datura showed what the choker does: she gave one to a captured Drakkari scout, who was delighted with it until it made him one of the Scourge. Such a device takes great effort to make and is never wasted on a random target: the Scourge wanted its finder.

Stefan turned the snare around. From abomination guts and ghoul drool he worked the choker into a disguise that let its wearer walk among the Scourge unnoticed, though the blightguards could see through it and it might fail without warning.

The plan was likely a death sentence. Disguised, the chosen one went up to Voltarus to win Drakuru's trust, and came back alive to report, much to Stefan's surprise. From then on every errand for Drakuru carried a second task for the Ebon Blade.

So the work went on under Drakuru's nose. Blight cauldrons were diluted until whole batches were useless, samples of his blight crystals were stolen, and his scourgewagons were blown apart, while each errand brought Stefan closer to knowing Drakuru's mind.
sources: quest 12686 description (Drakuru blames Darmuk for the ruined blight)

parts.body: At last Stefan ended the charade before Drakuru's creations could be unleashed. He modified the scepter Drakuru had given his servant so that it could turn the Blightbloods against their master. It was done, and the Ebon Blade's work in Zul'Drak grew that much easier.

title: Quetz'lun's Revenge
body: Har'koa could sense that something was wrong with Quetz'lun, the wind serpent goddess, but not what. Her altar had been overrun with powerful creatures. So Har'koa sent a mortal to find out, riding on the back of one of the very kittens that mortal had freed, the two of them meant to slip into the altar grounds unseen, see what had become of the goddess and come safely back. The kitten was glad of the chance to repay the one who had saved it, and warned its rider to hold on tight.
notes: ACCEPT 12665. Part 1 DONE 12665, part 2 DONE 12668 (after 12672; the underworld, phase 51671, told in the past tense since it lasts only until 12675 is turned in), part 3 DONE 12685. The Altar of Quetz'lun entry 6619 tells the lasting protection. Checked: underworld phase confirmed (51671 Ghostly, phase 2 in 4325, quest_start 12667 status complete or rewarded, until 12675 rewarded); part 2 is past tense on DONE 12668. The prophet is slain by the champion (12685 objective), not dead of the draining.

parts.body: Quetz'lun was dead, slain at her altar, and her prophet saw the kitten and its rider as they fled. Yet Har'koa sensed that all was not as it seemed: the goddess's spirit lingered in an underworld beneath the altar.

With sacred adornments taken from her own subduers, Har'koa sent her champion across into that underworld. Quetz'lun's spirit had cursed her worshippers as she died and dragged them down to torment forever. She set the mortal to slaughter them at her soul fonts and gather fragments of her curse's power, all for revenge on her prophet.

Her high priests were hexed and slain, and with a portion of Har'koa's spirit and a ritual at her corpse, Quetz'lun was drawn back into the world. She tore her power back out of her prophet, who screamed that it could not be taken, and drained, he was slain.

title: The Champion of Anguish
body: Gurgthock calls himself a fight promoter and his challengers the entertainment. Bring friends, he says, and he will set up the match: the first opponent is Yggdras. Fighters who once won the Ring of Blood in Nagrand are a great draw. Every bout pays, if the challenger lives. Gurgthock goes wherever the gold is, he admits, even to a place whose trolls he finds dirtier than ogres, and it is his troll bodyguard Wodin who hands each winner the purse.
sources: quest 12954 description and reward text (past champion of the Ring of Blood; forfeited the title)
notes: ACCEPT 12932 and 12954 (ExclusiveGroup 12932: 12954 for those who finished Nagrand's 9977). Part 1 on DONE 12933, 12934, 12935, 12936 (each bout's own turn-in, each telling its own foe; the part tells the run of foes in order, so only the triggers that reveal all of it are kept: DONE 12936 as the turn-in after the others), part 2 on DONE 12948. Nagrand's Ring of Blood is not retold. Checked: the jormungar and Gurgthock's stumbling over its name come from the fight itself, not the accept; the opening now names only Yggdras.

parts.body: The bouts grew wilder. After Yggdras came Stinkbeard, a magnataur lord out of the Dragonblight, then a lord of the elemental planes, then Orinoko Tuskbreaker, a tuskarr fisherman turned mercenary who fought with seals and penguins, and then Korrak the Bloodrager, champion of the Winterax trolls of Alterac, whom Gurgthock remembered from his days with the Frostwolf Clan.

The last challenger came from the Savage Ledge of Icecrown: Vladof the Butcher, a vrykul champion, riding his mammoth Enormos. When he fell, Gurgthock hailed a new Champion of Anguish, and announced that he was off to blow his winnings in the Underbelly of Dalaran.
